classification.difficultyReason: Use nonnegativity to simplify the absolute value of a square root, connect the resulting rule to its graph and restrictions, and explain why reversing the composition gives an empty real domain.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find $f(g(x))$, state its domain and range, and sketch its graph.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=-5-|\sqrt{x}|\\f(g(x))&=-5-\sqrt{x},\qquad x\ge0\end{align*}$$Since $\sqrt{x}\ge0$, the range is $y\le-5$. Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ in the $x$-axis, then translate it down 5 units. The graph starts at $(0,-5)$ and decreases to the right.

spec.description: Authored equation-driven solution sketch with closed endpoint at (0,-5), decreasing to the right.
spec.mathematics: y=-5-sqrt(x), x>=0; no x-intercept; y-intercept -5; no asymptote.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain why $g(f(x))$ is the empty function.

answer.short: $f(x)=-5-|x|<0$ for every real $x$, so $\sqrt{f(x)}$ is never real.
answer.worked: $$g(f(x))=\sqrt{-5-|x|}.$$Since $|x|\ge0$, the radicand satisfies $-5-|x|\le-5<0$. There is no real input for which the composite is defined, so its domain is empty.
